service_account.create.scope: Use the canonical namespace/project path. Authorization is repository scoped; a Broker resource ID is not a provider locator.
service_account.create.provisioning: Requires operator-enabled provisioning, this exact repository action grant and the selected GitLab actor's upstream permissions. Disabling provisioning also disables metadata reads and revocation through Broker; it does not revoke tokens already issued.
service_account.create.workflow: Create the account, retain result.serviceAccount.id, set membership with service_account.member.set, then issue a token with service_account.token.create. Each step is separately authorized; later failure leaves earlier successful steps in place. Do not recreate the account to retry a later step.
service_account.create.recovery: An uncertain mutation response remains applied_unverified with only established numeric IDs; reconcile the account ID before considering another mutation. A proven unsent write is the only not_applied/retrySafe:true case.

service_account.token.create.scope: Use the canonical namespace/project path. Authorization is repository scoped; a Broker resource ID is not a provider locator.
service_account.token.create.provisioning: Requires operator-enabled provisioning, this exact repository action grant and the selected GitLab actor's upstream permissions. Disabling provisioning also disables metadata reads and revocation through Broker; it does not revoke tokens already issued.
service_account.token.create.issuedCredential: Requires explicit future UTC expiresAt within operator limits and an eligible stored token/service credential; delegated OAuth cannot execute these token-only actions. Only the new downstream credential appears in result.issuedToken, alongside accessToken metadata. Broker execution credentials remain private. Sensitivity markers are advisory: use private delivery; later use follows GitLab permissions, not Broker grants.
service_account.token.create.recovery: An uncertain response uses applied_unverified at mutation_response with only safe numeric IDs. Metadata reads cannot recover the secret. Inspect the account/token list and revoke or reconcile a possibly issued credential before retrying; no automatic rollback or replay occurs.
service_account.token.create.ownership: The project service-account endpoint must prove userId belongs to this project. An ordinary user or another project's account cannot be substituted.
service_account.token.create.membership: Requires existing direct membership within the configured role cap; it does not change membership. Higher-role accounts may still have tokens revoked through the separately granted revoke action.

webhook.create.scope: Use the canonical namespace/project path. Authorization is repository scoped; a Broker resource ID is not a provider locator.
webhook.create.webhookScope: Project hooks only. The action needs its own Broker repository grant and the selected GitLab actor's webhook permission; the Broker does not track hook ownership.
webhook.create.configuration: url and events are required; events is the complete enabled event set. The operator destination allowlist must permit the new URL. Plain HTTP needs an explicit http rule; starting disabled HTTPS verification needs the separate operator setting. token/signingToken are sensitive inputs, never returned values.
webhook.create.recovery: The Broker verifies observable hook state after mutation. Any failed readback after acceptance uses applied_unverified with the safe hook ID, including a newly returned create ID; inspect it before deciding on another write.

webhook.custom_header.delete.secret: Delete one named custom header without supplying its secret value. Requires GitLab 17.1+.
webhook.custom_header.delete.recovery: Observable header-state readback proves the mutation. Ambiguity/readback failure uses applied_unverified with the safe hook ID, never the header key or value.
